title: Turtle Beach’s Vulcan II XP Is a Flashy Keyboard With a Flawed Finish
gist: WIRED rates Turtle Beach's $150 wired, full-size Vulcan II XP gaming keyboard 6/10. It has hot-swappable Titan HS linear or tactile switches, a 1,000-Hz polling rate and a strong macro manager in the Swarm II app. On the review unit, a cheap plastic base, an inverted media wheel and faulty LEDs made it feel middle-of-the-pack. It also drops the Hall effect keys of the earlier Vulcan II TKL Pro.

insights.claim: Turtle Beach's Vulcan II XP is a $150 wired-only full-size mechanical keyboard connected by a detachable 1.8 m USB-C to USB-A cable. A wireless Vulcan II XP Air version is launching for $50 more.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: Charging extra for wireless shows how Turtle Beach tiers prices in its Vulcan range.

insights.claim: The Vulcan II XP uses hot-swappable switches instead of the Hall effect keys of Turtle Beach's earlier Vulcan II TKL Pro. Its switches are rated for 50 million keystrokes, a third of the TKL Pro's 150 million.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: The newer product trades down on switch technology, which suggests cost cutting to hit the price point.

insights.claim: The Vulcan II XP offers a 1,000-Hz polling rate (1-ms response), which is competition-grade but falls short of higher-end 8,000-Hz keyboards.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: 8,000-Hz polling is now the premium benchmark in gaming peripherals.

insights.claim: Turtle Beach's Swarm II app supports per-key remapping, five onboard profiles, per-LED lighting and a millisecond-level macro manager with presets for games like Counter-Strike, Overwatch and Skyrim, plus office apps and Photoshop.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: Software ecosystems are the main differentiator and lock-in tool for peripheral makers.
insights.locator: Critical to the keyboard’s gaming credentials

insights.claim: Swarm II's ReacTap feature assigns two commands to one key. WIRED warns it may be banned in some competitive scenes under automation rules.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: Esports rules on automation limit how far peripheral makers can push software features.
insights.quote: This might be banned in some competitive scenes under automation rules, though.

insights.claim: WIRED's Vulcan II XP review unit had a media wheel that was inverted by default even after a firmware update, and NumPad LEDs stuck on white. Its brushed-aluminum top plate hides a cheap-feeling plastic basin underneath.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: QC problems in a mid-tier launch point to execution risk at Turtle Beach.

insights.claim: WIRED rates the Vulcan II XP 6/10. It calls it a decent first mechanical keyboard with pro-tier features, but says more demanding or professional players should aim higher.
insights.speaker: Matt Kamen
insights.so_what: The product is positioned for the mainstream upgrade market rather than the pro esports segment.
